deviations: D1: System actor representation — added UserRole.System enum member. The existing UserRole enum stored as string required no EF migration (enum-as-string convention; adding a new member only adds a new string value to the DB, which is backward-compatible). Actor.System is a static property returning an Actor with Role=UserRole.System and null UserId/DriverId. OrderEvent.ActorRole persists UserRole.System for Timeout events. No null-convention chosen; the enum approach is type-safe and explicit.

D2: PriceOverridden is a second OrderEvent row written ALONGSIDE Completed (not a separate transition). TransitionResult.Events carries 1 or 2 events. This contradicts the SKILL.md 'exactly one row' checklist item but follows the data model (OrderEventType.PriceOverridden exists) and the required test 'PriceOverridden event exists'. Documented supersession of the skill checklist.

D3: NewOrderOfferedAsync is defined on IRealtimePublisher but OrderService does NOT call it. The method requires FleetSettings.OfferTimeoutSeconds to compute expiresAt, which OrderService does not load. WI-13 (SignalR hub) and WI-14 (OfferTimeoutJob) are the callers.

D4: Registration follows the per-feature extension pattern: AddOrders() registers scoped OrderService; AddRealtime() registers singleton NoOpRealtimePublisher. Program.cs calls both. WI-13 swaps the publisher by modifying AddRealtime() body only.

D5: FleetAdmin treated as Dispatcher-equivalent throughout the state machine. This matches the DispatcherOnly authorization policy (rules/authorization.md) which already includes FleetAdmin. Without this, WI-09 endpoints would silently reject FleetAdmin actors.

D6: Order not found in OrderService.TransitionAsync returns TransitionResult.Failure(NotEntitled) not a thrown exception. NotEntitled maps to no-leak 404 in WI-09, which is the correct behavior for a missing order (consistent with the access-control no-leak principle).

D7: OrderEvent.FleetId is explicitly set to order.FleetId in MakeEvent() rather than relying on TaxiDbContext.SaveChanges auto-stamp. The auto-stamp is skipped when CurrentTenant.FleetId is null (WI-14 jobs run without a tenant context). Explicit assignment ensures correctness in both contexts.

D8: Cancel does NOT clear DriverId per the transition table ('Note: DriverId intentionally NOT cleared on cancel'). This preserves the audit trail — the event payload records the reason and the order retains the driver reference for historical reporting.
D9: Decline/Timeout clear DriverId/VehicleId/AssignedAt and persist the released driver ID in the event payload (declinedDriverId/timedOutDriverId) so auto-dispatch (v1.1) can skip that driver.

D10: Test isolation — integration tests use unique fleet per test (Guid-based suffix) instead of DB reset. No ResetDatabaseAsync exists on PostgresFixture. Tests seed their own fleet, users, vehicle, and driver to avoid cross-test contamination.

D11: AllowedFor does not enforce the 5-minute no-show rule (it cannot access the clock). Driver Cancel from Arrived appears in AllowedFor always; the runtime enforcement in ApplyCancel returns IllegalTransition before 5 minutes, and WI-09 endpoints map that to 409.

D12: NoWarn CS1591 added to Taxi.Api.Tests.csproj to suppress missing-XML-comment warnings on test methods, consistent with the test project being documentation-optional. All production code already carries XML docs.

D13: Actor changed from 'sealed class' to 'sealed record'. The original class was chosen to work around CS8958 (non-public parameterless ctor on record struct). A record class (not record struct) does not have that restriction. The change is purely a type-system improvement; all constructor and static-property code is unchanged.

D14: Driver no-show cancel enforces reason = 'no-show'. The deliverable requires: 'Driver: Arrived only, reason no-show, >= 5 min after ArrivedAt'. Any other reason string returns IllegalTransition. Test added: Apply_Cancel_ByDriver_WrongReason_ReturnsIllegalTransition.

Total new: 49. Previous total: 51. New total: 100. Key design choices: (1) System actor as UserRole.System enum (no null convention); (2) PriceOverridden as second event alongside Completed; (3) Driver status side effects carried in TransitionResult.DriverStatusChanges, applied by OrderService; (4) Version++ in OrderService immediately before SaveChangesAsync; (5) Publish-after-commit enforced by code ordering (publish calls after the try/catch SaveChanges block); (6) Concurrency failure caught at DbUpdateConcurrencyException boundary, not re-thrown. Red evidence: OrderStateMachineTests — 43 tests first ran from a compile-error (Actor struct private-ctor issue, XML doc issues); first green run showed 1 failure (Apply_Accept_FromWrongStatus test needed order.DriverId set); fixed and all 43 green. OrderServiceTests — first run showed 5 failures (slug too long, then FK constraint on actor_user_id requiring real dispatcher user); fixed by seeding dispatcher user and using that userId in Actor; then concurrency test failed with sequential execution; fixed by pre-loading order in scope2 before scope1 commits.
